changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 7 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`

- names `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — the console object page. The inline branch becomes `ganttViewOptions`, the sibling of `calendarViewOptions` and `timelineViewOptions`: the declared block spread whole, title floored at `'name'`, no date field invented. - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the render branch AND the capability gate. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

### `.changeset/7499-gantt-non-axis-floors-omitted.md`

- names `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the `object-gantt` render branch. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

### `.changeset/7773-kanban-adapter-groupfield-write.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Who is NOT affected — the boundary is node-local.** Every VIEW-LEVEL `groupField` read is untouched and still live: it is a legacy alias of the spec's `groupByField` on the kanban *view config*, mapped by `normalize-list-view.ts`, and both adapters still resolve lanes through it (`ObjectView.tsx`'s `kanbanCfg.groupField ||`, `ListView.tsx`'s `groupByField || groupField`). Authoring `options.kanban.groupField` on a `list-view` or `object-view` keeps working exactly as documented in `packages/plugin-list/README.md`. `groupField` is dead only on the generated `object-kanban` NODE.

### `.changeset/7780-object-kanban-record-source.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`groupBy` is untouched and stays REQUIRED** (objectui#7322, PR #7774). A record source and a lane key are different questions: every lane-less document above is still refused at `groupBy`, and the two readings PR #7774 excluded from counting as a lane-less mode — the `dataSource` json fragment in `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` and `ListView.tsx`'s runtime-generated node — are asserted still-refused in the new pin. The retired `groupField` tombstone is likewise still refused by name.

### `.changeset/8990-object-kanban-groupby-optional.md`

- names `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` **generates** the node as `groupBy: laneField`. `objectDef` loads asynchronously, so `laneField` is `undefined` on every load until it lands, and stays `undefined` whenever the object offers no `stageField` hint and none of `status` / `stage` / `state` / `phase`. The renderer serves that node; both published faces refused it. - `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` documents an `object-kanban` node that is exactly `{ type, dataSource }`, with no `groupBy`. ⚠️ This one is weaker and is cited for what it is: that fragment is **still** refused after this change, at `RECORD_SOURCE_REQUIRED`, because `dataSource` is not a rung of the record-source ladder. It shows a lane-less board is a documented authoring; it is not a document this change admits.

### `.changeset/list-user-actions-collision-5398.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The harvest now reads the object block only. Both `userActions` read sites in `ListView.tsx` carry a comment naming the collision, and `__tests__/ListView.userActionsCollision.test.tsx` pins each clause of it: the two shapes, a producer that manufactures the view one, the harvest's blindness to it, and the projection that must keep the object's operand with a toolbar block — or an empty block — present on the view.

### `.changeset/listview-comment-pair-4559.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Two comment corrections in `ListView.tsx` (objectui#4559, objectui#4966). No runtime behaviour changes and the emitted bundle is byte-identical; the published `.d.ts` does change, which is why this is a `patch` rather than an empty frontmatter.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `50e41f738` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1463 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2045 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36125946247)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ad119b4c346d98b4d39dc7a1555e4324b105d924`

Refs: `refs/review/pr-10597` = `ad119b4c346d98b4d39dc7a1555e4324b105d924` (equals the PR's reported head). `refs/review/main` = `21d34d5e2eff7d41a52ff03e3703cebddf83c2d2`. Merge-base `f5178a2729959814264d41ac96130c83bbef4097`. Diff merge-base to head: 3 files, +309 / -8, 4 commits (fix `e41d5cd`, changeset `7ee0250`, typing `61e16e5`, merge of `origin/main` `f5178a2` as `ad119b4`). Every line below was read with `git show refs/review/pr-10597:PATH`; the shared checkout was not entered or edited. The `os-dev-report` comment was not used as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) The fix, in the ruled shape.** Triage `5829668693` binds: 「measure first whether the count bar draws on a dataset chart; then objectui#10326's shape (derive the applied filter as empty while withheld, keep the held state, re-apply on switch back).」 At head `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` L1515-1522 derives `appliedFilters` (the module constant `WITHHELD_FILTER_GROUP`, L691, while `datasetChartOnScreen` and the held group has at least one row; otherwise the held `currentFilters` itself) and `appliedUserFilterConditions` (`WITHHELD_USER_FILTER_CONDITIONS`, L692, while `datasetChartOnScreen` and the held chip array is non-empty; otherwise the held `userFilterConditions` itself). `datasetChartOnScreen` (L1171-1172) is unchanged and is the same primitive objectui#10477 defined. This is the `searchTerm` shape of objectui#10326 (L1251, `searchlessViewOnScreen ? '' : searchInput`) applied to the Filter half: the held state is a separate value, the applied value is derived. Right against the card and the triage.
- **(b) Readers switched to the applied value.** The fetch's `buildEffectiveFilter` call (L2190) and the fetch effect's dependency list (L2699); the server export's `buildEffectiveFilter` (L4000) and its dependency list (L4102); `pageResetSignature` (L2710); `selfQueryFilter` (L3078); the grid empty-state `hasActiveQuery` (L4969-4970). Judged one by one: the fetch is the reader the card names and is the fix; the export mirrors the fetch by the file's own rule (L3998 「The same three filter sources as the data fetch」, and the client export writes `data`, L4053, which is the fetch's answer); `pageResetSignature` and `hasActiveQuery` follow the 10326 shape, where the same two readers were moved to the derived term. `selfQueryFilter` is behaviour-neutral: its consumers are the gantt node (L3445), the tree node (L3569) and the object-bound chart node (L3633), on all of which `datasetChartOnScreen` is false so applied equals held by identity, and the dataset chart node (L3600-3612) carries no `filter` at all. Nothing not asked was done; the reader switches are the derivation being read, not a second change.
- **(c) Held state kept, host write-back untouched.** The only writers of the held state are `setCurrentFilters` inside the FilterBuilder's `onChange` (L4366-4369, which is also the only caller of `onFilterChange`) and `setUserFilterConditions` handed to `UserFilters` (L4217). No effect touches either on a view change, so a switch into or out of the dataset chart neither clears the group nor tells the host to. The builder's `value` (L4365), the trigger's `hasFilters` highlight and badge (L3654, L4346-4353) and `UserFilters` (L4212-4221) still read the held state, which is right: none of them renders while the dataset chart is on screen (the L1228-1229 gate), and on a switch back they show the group that is applied again. Matches the triage's 「keep the held state, re-apply on switch back」.
- **(d) The toolbar gate is untouched.** The `showFilters` / `showUserFilters` lines (L1228-1229) and the `toolbarFlags` memo are not in the diff, as the claim's ⛔ required. `schema.filter` (the view's own filter) is still the first argument at every `buildEffectiveFilter` site, so the authored scope is not withheld: right, since objectui#10327's ruling concerns the user's controls and `ListViewSchema` already refuses an authored filter on a dataset chart.
- **(e) The "measure first" gate, verified at source.** The fetch effect (L2120 onward) is gated only by `ganttOwnsData` (L2163) and `objectDefLoaded` (L2171), so it runs on a chart view. The record-count bar (L5139) renders when `surfaceDrawsFetchedRows` (L2118, `currentView !== 'gantt'`) and rows are present, so it draws on a dataset chart and reads `serverTotal ?? data.length` (L5150). Both halves hold, so the finding does not reduce to wasted narrowing and the fix is owed. The pin's case 3 (test L172-182) asserts the same two facts before asserting the fix, so the measurement is pinned, not only reported.
- **(f) No re-query with nothing held (objectui#7394 class).** Each source is swapped only when it holds something (L1516, L1520). With nothing held both applied values keep the identity of the state they were derived from, so the fetch effect, which lists them (L2699) and not `currentView` (its L2663 comment says so by design), does not re-run on the switch. Pinned as case 6 (test L231-245). With something held, the identity flips to the module constant and back, which is exactly the two re-fetches the card asks for.
- **(g) Existing pins.** The diff edits or deletes no existing test. The sibling pins `ListView.datasetChartToolbarFilter-10327.test.tsx` and `ListView.searchWithheldTreeChart-10326.test.tsx` are untouched, and CI's eight test shards are green at the head.
- **(h) New pins can fail.** `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.datasetChartAppliedFilter-10512.test.tsx`, 6 cases; the fake data source (L93-110) answers each query from the fields its `$filter` names, so the count bar reads a different number for a narrowed query. Lit controls: case 1 (L156, grid, restored group narrows, bar reads `1 record`), case 2 (L163, object-bound chart, restored group narrows) and case 6 (L231, no re-query) pass at base and at head, and each is sensitive: case 2 goes red if the withhold keys on `currentView === 'chart'` alone, case 1 if it keys on everything, case 6 if the swap is unconditional (the identity flip re-runs the fetch effect, which lists `appliedFilters`). Negative legs, by reading against the base file: case 3 (L172) asserts every host `$filter` is undefined, and the base fetch sends `["status","=","open"]`; case 4 (L184) asserts every `$filter` equals the base filter alone, and the base sends the base filter combined with the user's; case 5 (L196) waits for a chart fetch whose `$filter` is undefined, and at base the switch re-issues no query, so the last call still names `status` and the wait times out. Not vacuous: the `every` assertions at L179 and L192 follow a `toHaveBeenCalled` wait (L177, L190), so the call list is non-empty; every case first awaits its view's stand-in. Case 5 also pins the re-application on the switch back (L222) and that `onFilterChange` was never called (L228). I did not run the suite (git-only rule); the head's CI is the independent signal.
- **(i) Nothing asked is missing.** Measure first: done and pinned (e). Fix shape: done (a). Pin that a restored filter does not narrow the fetch and the count on a dataset chart and does again on grid: cases 3, 5 and 1. One `.changeset/10512-…md`: present. File surface equals the claim: `ListView.tsx`, one pin beside the two sibling pins, one changeset.
- **(j) Source prose added by the diff, checked.** The docblock addition at L1156-1163 (「Two readers, one answer: the toolbar flags below, and the APPLIED user filter … The held state itself is kept … `schema.filter` … stays applied」) and the derivation comment at L1508-1514 are each true of the code beside them. The L686-690 comment on the constants (「every render hands the fetch effect the same identity」) is true. No README or `content/docs` prose is added, and the card asked for none.
- **(k) One observation, not a defect.** The derivation reads `userFilterConditions.length` unguarded (L1520) where the older empty-state reader guarded with `Array.isArray` (L4969).
